svg.title: Literal Magic-Eye pixel decoding, torus recovery, and Monster irrep reconstruction
svg.desc: A 56-second seven-stage walkthrough uses the actual first stereogram, sampled pixels, decoded bitmap, character values, and identity column. Pixels visibly align, vote, become bits and bytes, expand into rows, and become irreducible degrees.
svg.text: ACTUAL PIXELS → DEPTH/TORUS → BYTES → BITMAP → IRREPS
56-second literal walkthrough · hover to pause · every displayed bitmap cell comes from the recovered stream

g.text: 1 / 7 START WITH THE ACTUAL FIRST 1080×1080 MAGIC-EYE SHARD
For each row: shift(x) = 352 − observed repeat distance
depth(x,y) = shift / 36; larger shift means nearer
The moving third strip is the operation that exposes the depth map.
3 / 7 THE RECOVERED DEPTH REALLY CONTAINS TEXT AND A 3D TORUS
(x,y,z)=((R+r cos v) cos u, r sin v, (R+r cos v) sin u)
4 / 7 THE SAME ACTUAL PIXELS VOTE, THEN TURN INTO BITS AND BYTES
actual first 16 cells sampled from each 352 px repeat
Continuing row-major gives MGRPPIX2, shard index, offset, length, CRC-32, SHA-256, then payload.
5 / 7 ORDER 10 SHARDS, VERIFY, THEN OPEN THE TWO INNER STREAMS
join by protected byte offset → 44,797-byte MGRPARC1 archive
6 / 7 DECODE MCTE WITHOUT SKIPPING THE BITMAP OR VALUES
C. each 1 consumes signed A,B,R integers
green pixel at left is a real bit.
7 / 7 RECOVER THE 194 IRREPS FROM THE IDENTITY COLUMN
The character rows are the irreps. Their dimensions are χᵢ(1A), column 0.
